events.text: A clerk of the Ministries comes down the White Stairs with a ledger bound in cloud-silk, and writes {b8oh_house} into it in ink that does not dry. "Ten lines to a soul," the clerk says, bored. "You have used one. Mind the spelling; it follows you."

choices.text: Ask who reads such a ledger

effects.log: "Whoever you are next," says the clerk, and goes up the stairs again. You stand a long time on the same step.

choices.text: Check the spelling twice

effects.log: It is spelled right. The clerk, passing back down an hour later, nods at you as one nods at a rare competent person.

events.text: On the night your gate-lantern is first lit, an old drifting immortal in a borrowed boat calls across the clouds that lanterns on the Isles remember who lit them. You laugh. The flame leans, very slightly, toward you, and stays leaning.

choices.text: Raise a cup to the old drifter

effects.log: The boat is already lost in cloud. You drink alone to {b8oh_house}, and the flame bows again.

choices.text: Set a second lantern beside it

effects.log: Two flames, one leaning. By dawn it is hard to say which of them was lit first.

events.text: Under the rail of the lowest white stair of {b8oh_house} you cut the crest with your own thumbnail and a sliver of spirit stone, where nobody will see it for a hundred years. Whatever happens to your name, the stair now knows it.

choices.text: Press your palm to the cut

effects.log: The stone is warm for a breath and then ordinary. It is done, whatever it was.

choices.text: Cut a second small mark for luck

effects.log: Two marks. Anyone climbing in a century will wonder which hand was steadier.

events.text: The Ministries clerk lays down the brush. "There is no line left in your ledger for {b8oh_house}. Ten names, and every one of them still pulling at you. Either you let this one pass by, or you let the faintest of the ten go. I cannot choose for you."

choices.text: Let this one pass by

effects.log: You tell the clerk to close the page. The house will go on without your name on it, and without you owing it anything.

choices.text: Let the weakest of the ten go

effects.log: You turn the ledger and find the faintest line. The clerk wets the brush; the old name drifts out of you like smoke from a snuffed lamp.

events.text: A bell on the Rolls Terrace tolls once, which it does only when a soul tries to hold an eleventh house. A queue of disciples turns to look. The clerk smiles with half a face. "The ledger has no mercy and no more room. Which will it be?"

choices.text: Leave {b8oh_house} unwritten

effects.log: You step out of the line. The bell is quiet, and the house keeps its roof without your name on the rafter.

choices.text: Strike out the weakest of the ten

effects.log: The clerk draws one thin line through the faintest name. You feel a stairway you once climbed let go of your sleeve.

choices.text: Ask for a night to think

effects.log: "Ten years," says the clerk, "is a night to us." The bell tolls again then, in the empty hall, when you are gone.

events.text: The wind-boat captain is bragging of every isle on the run, and when she reaches {b8oh_house} her hands go quiet on the rudder. "Founded by {b8oh_founder}, they say. {b8oh_gens} heads since. The gate-stairs are the steepest I have ever seen, and the tea is good." You have never been there. You know the tea.

choices.text: Ask her to set you down there

effects.log: She shrugs and trims the sail. By evening the white stairs rise out of the cloud, steeper than you remember.

choices.text: Ask for the next isle instead

effects.log: She shows no surprise. You watch the isle drop behind, lantern-lit, and do not wave.

events.text: Among the spirit-stone tithe lists nailed to a ferry post is a line for {b8oh_house}: still paying, still standing, {b8oh_gens} heads old. Someone has written beside it, in an old hand, "ask for the cook." Your thumb is on the name before you know it.

choices.text: Take the ferry toward it

effects.log: The ferryman does not ask why. He says only that the isle is worth the climb and always was.

choices.text: Leave the list to the wind

effects.log: The nail holds. The paper rustles. You walk off with the tune of a founding song in your head and no idea where you learned it.

events.text: A scholar-immortal on the Sea of Clouds ferry is reading aloud from a guide to the minor houses. "{b8oh_house}: a middling house, a loyal gate. They keep the first tablet before every other in their hall and will not say whose it is." The scholar glances up. "You are very still, friend."

choices.text: Say you were only listening

effects.log: The scholar nods and turns the page. For the rest of the crossing you do not hear one more word of the guide.

choices.text: Ask which isle, and how long the stair

effects.log: The scholar tells you, with relish, and draws the stairs in the air with two fingers. You will be able to find them in the dark.

events.text: Your guest-cup in the tea pavilion has a glaze you know. The potter's mark is that of {b8oh_house}. The server says their disciples sell the cups at the ferry landing to pay the stone tithe, and that the house is {b8oh_step}. You hold the cup to the light as if it could be weighed.

choices.text: Ask the way to its landing

effects.log: The server points down the clouds with a tray. "Third lantern, left of the heron." You finish your tea as slowly as you can.

choices.text: Buy two cups, and go the other way

effects.log: You pay and leave by the far stair. The cups sit on your shelf, and the house sits in your mind, and neither speaks.

events.text: The gatekeeper of {b8oh_house} bows you into the first hall without asking your name. Before the altar of ancestors stands one tablet, first among all, its lettering older than the house's oldest tree. It says {b8oh_founder}. Your breath goes out of you like a bellows.

choices.text: Give your name, as any guest would

effects.log: You give a plain name and ask to be shown to the guest-seats. The keeper writes it down without looking at the tablet, which you appreciate.

choices.text: Say the tablet is yours

effects.log: You say it out loud, there in the hall, under the lanterns. The keeper looks from the tablet to your face, and sends a boy running.

choices.text: Bow to the tablet and go back down

effects.log: You bow to it as a stranger would, then once more as no stranger would. The stairs take you down gently.

events.text: The stair is as steep as you knew it would be, and your knees know where each worn step dips. At the top, children are sweeping petals from the first-hall threshold and singing a counting song you are certain has a verse about you. Inside, the tablet of {b8oh_founder} stands first, polished.

choices.text: Ask for a guest's seat

effects.log: A sweeper-child takes your sleeve and leads you in solemnly, as to a great lord. You do not correct the child.

choices.text: Tell the sweepers who you were

effects.log: The children go quiet. The smallest says, very carefully, that the founder died long ago. You say you know, and that it is a long story.

choices.text: Sweep a few petals with them and go

effects.log: Nobody asks you to stay and nobody asks you to go. At the bottom stair you realise you are humming the verse.

events.text: Rain on the cloud-sea, and the gate-keeper of {b8oh_house} has come out under an oiled umbrella to look at you. Behind them the first hall glows. "Whoever you are," the keeper says, "the tablet at the head of our hall has been unusually warm since you stepped onto the stair."

choices.text: Say you only seek shelter from the rain

effects.log: The keeper holds the umbrella over you across the whole courtyard and asks nothing. You are seated by the brazier with a bowl of broth.

choices.text: Say the tablet knows you

effects.log: The keeper's eyebrows rise and stay risen. "Then you will not mind," the keeper says, "if the elders ask you a few things."

choices.text: Thank the keeper and go back into the rain

effects.log: The umbrella follows you to the gate, and then stops. You do not look back, and feel it watching.

events.text: A feast day. The gate of {b8oh_house} is wide and strangers are welcome to the long tables in the first court. You eat and say little. Then the cups go round to the head of the hall, to the first tablet, and each disciple pours a drop upon the floor before it. {b8oh_founder}. It is your hand your cup is in.

choices.text: Stay and join the table

effects.log: You sit through the toasts as a guest, and when they ask what you do you say you have had many trades. They find that funny.

choices.text: Pour the drop with them, and name yourself

effects.log: You pour, and the hall goes quiet, and you say the name on the tablet. It sounds odd in your mouth, like a tooth that returned.

choices.text: Slip out before the second toast

effects.log: You are down three stairs when the singing begins behind you. It is the founding song. You know the harmony part.

events.text: The elders of {b8oh_house} laugh until one has to be helped to a chair. "The founder, is it? We have had three founders this year already, one of them a goat-herd." A disciple wipes tears off the bridge of the nose. Nobody means harm. It is the worse for that.

choices.text: Laugh with them, and say no more

effects.log: You laugh with them, and they like you better for it. Some part of you notes that this is also how a tablet goes cold.

choices.text: Insist, and raise your voice in the hall

effects.log: Your voice rings under the beams. The head elder stops laughing. Within the hour you are being shown the door with every courtesy and no appeal.

choices.text: Bow, and ask to see the first tablet again

effects.log: They let you, amused. You stand before the lettering a long time. It does not hurt to be laughed at once you have stood there.

events.text: At the guest table, a young disciple of {b8oh_house} asks you to say your claim again, slowly, for the others, and by the second half the whole row is wheezing. "And did you also build the stairs?" "Did the stairs build you?" Your tea has gone cold.

choices.text: Take the teasing and finish your tea

effects.log: You do, and they refill it twice out of embarrassment. By the end you are somewhere between a joke and a friend.

choices.text: Stand, and say they will regret this

effects.log: You say it more sharply than you meant. The laughter dies. By morning your guest-room has been given to someone else.

events.text: The head of {b8oh_house}, {b8oh_head}, does not laugh. {b8oh_head} sets a bowl of clear water before you, a brush and an old scroll with a gap in it. "The founder left a line unfinished. Finish it, and we shall see what you are."

choices.text: Write the line from memory

effects.log: The brush knows the stroke before you do. {b8oh_head} reads it, says nothing, and has the bowl taken away.

choices.text: Decline to be tested by a scroll

effects.log: You say your name should not need a brush. {b8oh_head} bows, a hair lower than before. The hall does not decide, and nor do you.

choices.text: Ask what the line should say

effects.log: {b8oh_head} smiles for the first time. "That," {b8oh_head} says, "is the first wise thing a pretender has not done."

events.text: They bring you down to the cistern under the first hall, where the house's oldest ritual is kept: a lamp, a cup and a question. {b8oh_head} asks what the founder drank on the night the house was named. The only light is the lamp and your face in the water.

choices.text: Answer from the heart

effects.log: You say a rough tea of mountain pine, bitter. {b8oh_head} gives no sign, but the old cup beside the lamp is turned to face you.

choices.text: Say you do not remember, and it is true

effects.log: The honesty seems to count for something. "Few say that," {b8oh_head} murmurs, and the lamp burns a little steadier.

events.text: The old gate-keeper of {b8oh_house} comes to you after the elders have gone to bed, and kneels, which at that age is not easy. "I swept the first tablet every dawn for sixty years," the keeper says. "It has never moved the way it moved when you spoke. I believe you. So will they, by spring."

choices.text: Raise the keeper and accept the belief

effects.log: You lift the keeper up by both elbows. The house, from that night, speaks of you as one speaks of a tide long due.

choices.text: Ask the keeper to say nothing yet

effects.log: The keeper agrees, and keeps the secret for a month, which for a gate-keeper is a heroic length of time.

events.text: {b8oh_head} puts away the scroll before you have finished the answer. "That is the founder's cadence," says {b8oh_head}. "We changed the third beat in the song a hundred years ago and nobody ever told me what it was before. You have just sung it." The elders say nothing; one weeps.

choices.text: Take the head's hand and let them believe

effects.log: You take it. The elders' voices come back slowly, like geese, and by evening a guest-room is being aired for you.

choices.text: Say you are only a guest who knew the song

effects.log: {b8oh_head} nods very slowly, as one nods to a kind lie, and does not forget it.

events.text: After years at the table of {b8oh_house} the elders make you an offer in the first court, under all the lanterns: the rank of {b8oh_next}. It comes with a seat nearer the head and a vote on the spring tithe. A younger disciple watches, trying not to hope.

choices.text: Accept the rank

effects.log: You take it with both hands. The seat is harder than the guest seat, and the view of the stairs from it is better.

choices.text: Decline, and recommend the younger disciple

effects.log: You push the scroll across the table. The younger one is too stunned to speak. {b8oh_head} writes your recommendation down and says nothing at all.

choices.text: Decline, and stay as you are

effects.log: You say the seat is fine where it is. The elders agree it is a fine seat. The offer will not come twice soon.

events.text: A courier of the Ministries has been through, and {b8oh_house} has had its tithe confirmed. In the glow of that, the elders decide to raise you to {b8oh_next}. {b8oh_head} fastens a new cord on your sleeve and says, quietly, "this one was woven for you the year you arrived."

choices.text: Wear the cord

effects.log: It is lighter than it looks. By dusk the whole isle seems to be using your new title as if it had always been so.

choices.text: Ask whose hand wove it

effects.log: "A cook's," says {b8oh_head}. "Who is gone. The cook said you would be back."

choices.text: Hand the cord back with thanks

effects.log: You hold it out. {b8oh_head} takes it carefully, as a sacred thing, and puts it in a box that is clearly meant to wait.

events.text: The whole hall of {b8oh_house} is cold with fog on the morning the elders raise you to {b8oh_next}. It is meant to be a quiet thing, but the cooks have made a cake in the shape of a stair. Someone has put a tiny figure at the top of it, and the figure is you.

choices.text: Cut the cake and take the rank

effects.log: You cut the first slice for the gate-keeper. The rank settles on you like a warm coat, and fits.

choices.text: Thank them, and say not yet

effects.log: They are crestfallen for exactly as long as it takes to pass the cake. Then they save the slice with the little figure for you.

events.text: Spring tithe at {b8oh_house}. The ledger is short by a little more than the isle can grow, and the elders eye you, the {b8oh_rank}, with the hope of those who do not like to ask. Lanterns hiss in the damp. Nobody is going to say it first.

choices.text: Offer counsel on the ledger

effects.log: You spend three evenings with the abacus and the cook's accounts, and find where the leak is. The elders pretend to be surprised.

choices.text: Take a quiet cut from the guest-fund

effects.log: No one stops you, because no one counts. The stones are yours by custom. The house is the poorer by it, and you know exactly by how much.

choices.text: Say you have outstayed your welcome

effects.log: You bow to each elder in turn. The cook, at the back, weeps openly into a towel. You go down the stairs at dawn.

events.text: A storm out of the Sea of Clouds pins the isle for nine days. At the long table of {b8oh_house}, a {b8oh_rank} has no great duty, only a seat and a bowl, and the quiet cleverness that people ask of guests. The head's children are restless and the elders have run out of stories.

choices.text: Tell the old stories the house has forgotten

effects.log: You tell them, and they are, startlingly, the house's own. The elders go quiet, then write them down.

choices.text: Eat well and say little

effects.log: The stores of the isle thin a little more. No one grudges it aloud. The storm clears and you are fatter, and the shelves are not.

choices.text: Use the lull to say goodbye

effects.log: You leave a note under the first tablet and board the first boat the storm allows. The tablet is warm when you set the note down.

events.text: Midautumn at {b8oh_house}. The lanterns are up. A young disciple with ink-stained fingers brings you a problem: the third form of the house's sword-song has been taught wrong for a generation, and nobody can say how it should go. The disciple looks at you, the {b8oh_rank}, as if you had it in your sleeve.

choices.text: Show the form as you remember it

effects.log: You show it in the court, slowly. Something in the stance rights itself. The young disciple stares and runs to fetch the others.

choices.text: Keep the form, and teach them the wrong one

effects.log: A small meanness. You teach them the old error with a straight face. For a month you feel the house lean away from you, then forget.

choices.text: Say you cannot, and take your leave

effects.log: You say you cannot teach what you cannot show, which is true in more than one way. You are on the evening boat.

events.text: A guest from a rival isle is at the table of {b8oh_house} tonight, eating the good tea and sizing up the gate. The head asks, with a smile that fools nobody, whether the {b8oh_rank} would care to sit beside the guest and keep the conversation harmless.

choices.text: Sit by the guest and steer the talk

effects.log: You spend three hours saying nothing of value, charmingly. The rival leaves with a poor map of the house.

choices.text: Sell the guest a small hint for a favour

effects.log: A hint for a favour, in the dark under the table. It is a smaller betrayal than most, and you carry it anyway.

choices.text: Excuse yourself and leave the table

effects.log: You rise and bow to the head, who sighs and lets you. Down the stairs you hear the rival laugh.

events.text: {b8oh_old_head} has gone to the long drift beyond the Isles, and the first hall of {b8oh_house} is full of people who each want a different successor. They look at you, the {b8oh_rank}, whose word the old head valued. The able deputy, {b8oh_head}, stands to one side. A kinsman stands to the other.

choices.text: Back {b8oh_head}, the able one

effects.log: You say it plainly, in the court, before all. The kinsman bows and does not hide his face. The house breathes out.

choices.text: Back the old head's kin

effects.log: Blood is blood, and the old head loved the child. You say so, and the hall makes the sound a hall makes when it agrees with the heart.

events.text: The cloud-bell is rung for {b8oh_old_head}, and the Ministries clerk waits on the stair with the roll, wanting a name by dusk. In the long quiet of the first hall every sleeve turns toward you. Two are in the running: {b8oh_head}, who has the skill, and a kinsman, who has the blood.

choices.text: Name the skilled one

effects.log: You say {b8oh_head}'s name and the clerk writes it. Whatever else the house is, it will not drift for lack of a hand on the oar.

choices.text: Name the kinsman

effects.log: You name the kinsman. The clerk writes it with a blank face. Some say you chose for love. You let them.

events.text: A pigeon-wind brings word to your sleeve that {b8oh_house} is {b8oh_step} now. A stair has lost its rail. The cook has left. The spring stone-tithe is two months overdue, and the last line of the letter says only, "if ever you are able."

choices.text: Send what you can, unsigned: {b8oh_help}

effects.log: You send it without a name. The letter that comes back is full of guesses about the donor, and nearly all of them wrong.

choices.text: Let it be

effects.log: You fold the letter. The house will do what houses do, with or without you. You do not read the last line again.

events.text: A boatman who has been to {b8oh_house} says it is {b8oh_step}. The boatman says it plainly, as one reports weather. The lanterns on the lower stair have not been lit in a month, and a family of herons has taken the cistern. Nobody expects you to do anything about it.

choices.text: Send help anonymously: {b8oh_help}

effects.log: You pay the boatman to carry it. The boatman says it will be said to come from the Ministries. You tell him that is fine.

choices.text: Let it be

effects.log: You thank the boatman and pay him for his news. The herons, you decide, will do the house no harm.

events.text: A note in a stranger's hand reaches you through three ferrymen: {b8oh_house} is {b8oh_step}. The writer signs as "a cook who was left behind." They do not ask for anything. They only say they thought you would want to know, and that the tablet is warm.

choices.text: Send a gift for the cook: {b8oh_help}

effects.log: The gift goes by the same three ferrymen. The cook's reply is a single recipe, in careful hand, for the tea you used to drink.

choices.text: Let it be

effects.log: You keep the note in the sleeve a month, then burn it in the lamp. The tablet does not say anything in your dreams.

events.text: The news reaches you on a ferry: {b8oh_house} has fallen. The isle has gone quiet, and its lanterns are out. A fellow passenger, not knowing, tells you the story as one tells a tale of the sea. At the end you thank them very evenly and ask the boatman to stop talking about the weather.

choices.text: Say a name for the first tablet, under your breath

effects.log: You say {b8oh_founder}, once, and the ferry rocks. Nobody turns. The sea-wind carries it off like any other word.

choices.text: Look at the cloud until it feels less

effects.log: You look at the cloud for a long time. It is not less. It is only cloud.

events.text: You wake at night with the taste of the old tea in your mouth and a sound like a stair-rail giving way. By morning a rumour is in every pavilion: {b8oh_house} is gone. You keep drinking your breakfast tea. Your hand is steady. The cup, for some reason, is not.

choices.text: Light one lantern for it

effects.log: You light a single small flame in the window. It leans, steadily, toward a direction where there is nothing to see.

choices.text: Go on with your day, and do not speak of it

effects.log: You go on with your day. In the evening you find you have set out an extra cup on the table, and you let it sit.

events.text: A scribe of the Book of Fates, ink to the elbow, adds {b8oh_house} to a page kept for you alone. "Ten lines to a soul. Every temple you raise stays on it after the gods have forgotten the temple." The page is warm, and the scribe will not meet your eye.

choices.text: Ask what happens when the page is full

effects.log: "It weighs on you, like a debt," says the scribe. You stand very straight for the rest of the day.

choices.text: Offer the scribe a cup of evening dew

effects.log: It is drunk as though no one had offered in a thousand years. Your line is written in a slightly better hand.

events.text: The first worshipper of {b8oh_house} is a ferrywoman who lights one stick of incense and says only, "I do not know what you are for. Please be for something." The smoke climbs, finds your wrist and ties itself there. The other gods look politely elsewhere.

choices.text: Answer her, though she cannot hear

effects.log: You tell the smoke you are for her ferry, her children, her bad knee. The thread goes warm.

choices.text: Follow the thread down to her hearth

effects.log: You watch her sleep from a corner of the sky. In the morning her prayers are shorter and surer.

events.text: A lesser god of thresholds drifts into your hall carrying a plate of rice cakes. "For the founding. I was not asked, but one hears." It sets the plate on your new altar, bows to the wrong wall, and whispers that your name is cut under the altar's foot where no knee wears.

choices.text: Eat a cake with the lesser god

effects.log: It is overjoyed, and talks for an hour about doors. You learn more than you expected.

choices.text: Ask to see the stone

effects.log: You are shown it at once. It is plain and well set, the right shape for a name to sleep in.

events.text: All ten of your altars ring at once in the Hall of Hours, a sound the keepers call the Tenfold Sigh. A clerk raises a brass scale. "Ten pull at you already. {b8oh_house} would be the eleventh. Let it pass, or put down the faintest of the ten. The scale cannot be cheated."

choices.text: Let {b8oh_house} pass

effects.log: The pan lifts. The clerk writes: "Declined by the founder." The altar goes on in other hands, owing you nothing.

choices.text: Put down the faintest of the ten

effects.log: The clerk fishes the lightest weight out with silver tongs. Far away, a small prayer goes quiet for good.

events.text: A worshipper of a god you do not know prays hard to {b8oh_founder}, and the prayer reaches a soul too full to hold it. It bounces back, hums in the air and annoys a passing archivist. "Your page has no room," the archivist says. "Choose: this one, or the dimmest of your ten."

choices.text: Send the prayer on, unanswered

effects.log: You wave it toward a better home. The humming stops. You feel faintly mean, and entirely sensible.

choices.text: Let the dimmest of your ten go dark

effects.log: The archivist scratches it out. You hear the sound a very old bell makes when it is taken down.

choices.text: Ask the archivist to hold it a night

effects.log: "A night in heaven is a decade below," says the archivist. "I will hold it. Do not make me regret it."

events.text: A prayer comes up the cloud-road and, through some error of the sorting wind, lands in your hand. It is addressed to {b8oh_founder}, from a keeper of {b8oh_house}, asking help with a leaking roof. The hand is shaky, the faith real, and the name at the top is yours.

choices.text: Walk down to see the roof

effects.log: You step off the cloud and follow the thread to a small temple. The roof is, in fact, leaking.

choices.text: Pass the prayer to the Hall of Roofs

effects.log: It is the only polite thing to do, and you feel no better for it.

events.text: Two minor gods share a bench at the divine exchange and grumble about their altars. One says {b8oh_house} is the best-kept cult in the south quarter, "{b8oh_gens} keepers old, and the incense is still the original blend." Your tongue knows the smell. You have never been.

choices.text: Ask the way to its altar

effects.log: They draw the road in smoke: down, left of a moon, a courtyard with a very old gate.

choices.text: Say nothing, and buy a stick of the blend

effects.log: It burns in your room all night, and the smoke rises in one quiet column.

events.text: The Book of Fates keeps an index of cults for the idle to leaf through. A line reads: "{b8oh_house}, founded by {b8oh_founder}, {b8oh_gens} keepers, {b8oh_step}." Beside it an old clerk has inked a tiny lamp. The ink is still wet, as if it had been waiting for a reader.

choices.text: Copy the road into your sleeve

effects.log: The clerk watches you do it and says nothing, with great tact.

choices.text: Close the index and file it away

effects.log: The book closes by itself, a little regretfully. You hold the place a moment longer than you need to.

events.text: A harvest-god at a feast of the Cheonho pantheon names the cults that owe it favours. "{b8oh_house}, now. Founded by a god nobody has met. Odd how warmly their worshippers say that old name." It pauses. "Do you know it?"

choices.text: Say you have heard of it

effects.log: It gossips on, delighted. You nod where you should, and your tea cools.

choices.text: Ask where its altar is kept

effects.log: You are told, with cheerful wrong turns and then the right one. You write it on your sleeve.

events.text: The temple keepers of {b8oh_house} have swept the court, filled the lamps and placed a clay tiger at the foot of the first name-stone, as though a visit were expected. The stone reads {b8oh_founder}. The senior keeper greets you at the gate and, remarkably, asks no name.

choices.text: Ask for a place among the guests

effects.log: A bowl is set out at once. A young worshipper asks mid-meal if you are one of the old gods. You say you are passing through.

choices.text: Touch the stone and say the name aloud

effects.log: The stone is warm under your palm. The keeper puts down the bowl and takes a long time about it.

choices.text: Leave a rice cake and go

effects.log: The keeper watches you down the road and, you think, whispers a short prayer after you.

events.text: A pilgrim crowd of five hundred is shuffling through the gate of {b8oh_house} for the offering day, and you go with it. At the first altar the keepers read the foundation aloud: "raised by {b8oh_founder}." A hush runs over the court, and every head bows toward an empty cushion beside you.

choices.text: Take a worshipper's cup and stay

effects.log: You are given a cup and a place on the long bench. No one knows the cushion is warm.

choices.text: Sit on the empty cushion

effects.log: A gasp crosses the court and dies. The reader stops mid-line. You sit very straight, and wait.

choices.text: Bow with the others and slip away

effects.log: Nobody looks up. By the end of the street you are walking in time with the drum.

events.text: Fog in the south quarter, and the doorkeeper of {b8oh_house} dozes by a lit lamp. "Whoever you are," the doorkeeper murmurs, waking, "the first name-stone began to hum an hour ago. It has not hummed since the founding."

choices.text: Ask for tea and a quiet seat

effects.log: The doorkeeper wakes fully and brings tea in a cup too good for a stranger. You sit under the hum until it settles.

choices.text: Say the hum is for you

effects.log: The tea is put down slowly. "Then you had better speak to the head," says the doorkeeper, "and sit when you do."

choices.text: Say it must be the fog, and go

effects.log: Behind you the hum rises a note, and falls again as you pass the gate.

events.text: In the first hall of {b8oh_house} a lesser god in borrowed robes is lecturing newcomers on the cult's history, pointing at the first name-stone with a feather. "Founder {b8oh_founder}! Utterly mysterious!" It turns, sees you, and drops the feather. The newcomers look from you to the stone.

choices.text: Pick up the feather and join the tour

effects.log: You follow the lecture to its end. The lesser god gets half the dates wrong, and you let it.

choices.text: Correct the lesser god, kindly

effects.log: You give the right date, and the right reason. The hall goes very still, and a keeper begins to hurry.

choices.text: Smile at the newcomers and leave

effects.log: The lesser god calls after you, mortified, that it meant no offence. You wave it off.

events.text: The head-keeper of {b8oh_house} is a patient god, and still laughs. "Founder of this cult, is it? Last winter a fox claimed the first altar for its den. Do have a rice cake." Nobody is unkind. Somehow that is worse.

choices.text: Take the rice cake and laugh gently

effects.log: The hall relaxes. It is a good cake. You eat it seated apart from the first altar.

choices.text: Say the altar will remember this

effects.log: The hall goes cold and the keepers rise. You are shown out with scrupulous politeness, and the gate lamp is put out.

choices.text: Ask to light a stick at the first altar

effects.log: They allow it, amused. Your smoke goes up clean and straight, and no one remarks on it.

events.text: A cluster of godlings at the refectory table of {b8oh_house} turns your claim into a children's rhyme, and by the third verse the room is singing it. The tune is cruel and catchy. You are expected to be a good sport.

choices.text: Sing the last verse yourself

effects.log: You sing it in a better key. They stare, then applaud, which is its own kind of defeat.

choices.text: Call the godlings to order, sharply

effects.log: Silence. By dark you have been moved from the guest wing to a hermit's cell on the cult's far rim.

events.text: {b8oh_head} of {b8oh_house} lights a wick before the first altar and asks: "Which prayer did the founder say last, on the night the first worshipper came?" There is only the flame to read your face.

choices.text: Say the prayer as it comes to you

effects.log: The words arrive in an old cadence. The flame leans, steadies, and keeps leaning toward you.

choices.text: Say you cannot recall, and mean it

effects.log: The flame shrinks and then brightens. {b8oh_head} murmurs that honesty is also a kind of prayer.

choices.text: Ask what the worshippers say it was

effects.log: {b8oh_head} smiles. "The worshippers have it wrong. I wonder if you know the right one."

events.text: Three offerings are set on the altar steps of {b8oh_house}: river water, a handful of ash, a ripe plum. {b8oh_head} says the founder always took the one forgotten longest. You may take one. Everyone in the chapel is carefully not watching.

choices.text: Take the bowl of river water

effects.log: It tastes of the south quarter at dawn. {b8oh_head} nods and says nothing further.

choices.text: Take the ash

effects.log: It is cold and fine between your fingers. The chapel exhales once.

choices.text: Take the plum and give half to {b8oh_head}

effects.log: The chapel breaks into quiet laughter. A test of that kind is rarely won, and never so.

events.text: The old incense-keeper of {b8oh_house} presses a worn cord into your palm: the founder's own, kept in cedar for six hundred years. "It stirred when you came. I believe you. The rest will follow by the next full moon."

choices.text: Take the cord and let them believe

effects.log: It fits your wrist as though made for it. From that night the house names you the founder returned.

choices.text: Give the cord back, and ask for time

effects.log: The keeper returns it to its box with a respectful slowness, and says it will keep.

events.text: A kneeling worshipper in the back of the hall of {b8oh_house} breaks into a hymn nobody has sung for six hundred years, and the keepers, one by one, find they know it. {b8oh_head} lays down the Book of the Altar. "You paused where the founder paused. We kept the words, but lost the pause."

choices.text: Accept the hall's belief

effects.log: A seat is cleared. For the first time in anyone's hearing the incense burns with a single steady flame.

choices.text: Say you only studied the Book

effects.log: {b8oh_head} nods like a god accepting a courteous lie, and does not forget it.

events.text: After a long season at the table of {b8oh_house}, the keepers lay a gold-thread ribbon before you: the rank of {b8oh_next}, a seat nearer the altar, a say in the autumn offerings. A young godling looks on, hands clasped.

choices.text: Accept the ribbon

effects.log: The seat is firmer than the guest bench, and the incense reaches it thicker.

choices.text: Decline, and name the godling instead

effects.log: You press the ribbon into the godling's palm. {b8oh_head} writes it down and tells no one how rare that is.

choices.text: Decline, and stay as you are

effects.log: You say the guest bench is warm enough. The offer will not return soon.

events.text: A pilgrimage of five hundred has just passed the gate of {b8oh_house}, and every offering bowl is full. In the glow of it the keepers raise you to {b8oh_next}. {b8oh_head} ties a tassel to your sleeve and says it was woven the year you first came down the road.

choices.text: Wear the tassel

effects.log: It is light as breath. By noon the whole cult uses your new title as if it had always been so.

choices.text: Ask who wove it

effects.log: "A faithful old woman, since gone," says {b8oh_head}. "She said you would come."

choices.text: Hand it back with thanks

effects.log: It is put in a cedar box that is clearly meant to wait.

events.text: The Book of Fates, with a flourish no one has seen from it before, writes you into the roll of {b8oh_house} as {b8oh_next}. The keepers learn of it as one learns of weather: a rustle, a chill, and then every lamp in the hall leaning toward you.

choices.text: Take the title with a bow

effects.log: The lamps settle. A senior keeper brings the new robe, folded over both arms.

choices.text: Ask the Book to wait a season

effects.log: The page flutters, and goes still. You feel it waiting, with some good humour.

events.text: Autumn offerings at {b8oh_house}: the bowls are thin. The keepers watch you, the {b8oh_rank}, with the hope of people who do not like to ask. Prayer-smoke clings low in the court, and no one wants to say first that the cult is short of faith.

choices.text: Offer counsel on the offering-roll

effects.log: Three evenings with the keepers, and you find the village that stopped sending rice. A letter goes out; the bowls are fuller by midwinter.

choices.text: Take a quiet portion of the guest offerings

effects.log: No one counts the guest portion. The faith in your hand is yours by custom, and the altar is the thinner by it.

choices.text: Say you should be going

effects.log: At the gate the spirit weeps into its sleeve. You go down the cloud-road at dawn.

events.text: A lesser god of crossroads has been given the seat beside the {b8oh_rank} at {b8oh_house}, and is rather overwhelmed by it. It asks, in whispers, how one speaks to a Head, which spoon to use, and whether a god may refuse a second cup. It has clearly been told you matter.

choices.text: Coach the lesser god through the meal

effects.log: By the sweet course it is a little less frightened. The keepers see, and note it kindly.

choices.text: Let it flounder, and enjoy the show

effects.log: It spills the soup. You smile into your cup. A small unkindness, unspoken, and you know it.

choices.text: Change seats and leave early

effects.log: You slip out through the side gate. The lesser god looks bereft, and then recovers and eats your dessert.

events.text: Midsummer, and the Evening Prayer of {b8oh_house} has three endings, each championed by a different elder. A young godling brings the quarrel to you, the {b8oh_rank}, hoping you hold the true one in your sleeve.

choices.text: Give the ending as you recall it

effects.log: A long falling line. The godling writes it on a leaf and runs. By dark every keeper is saying it.

choices.text: Give a wrong ending, as a joke

effects.log: It works for a week. Then the elders find out, and the cult remembers you less warmly.

choices.text: Say some endings must be found, not given

effects.log: True, and a little cowardly. You take the evening road down.

events.text: Midwinter, and the cult-house of {b8oh_house} is warm only around the first altar. The keepers draw lots for the sleeping places near it, and offer the {b8oh_rank} the best spot on grounds of guesthood. Several pairs of eyes follow the offer.

choices.text: Give your place to the weakest keeper

effects.log: You sleep in the draught. In the morning the oldest keeper presses your hand. The cult is warmer all year.

choices.text: Take the warm spot as offered

effects.log: You sleep soundly. The oldest keeper wakes coughing. You notice, and you do not mention it.

choices.text: Say you will not be a burden, and go

effects.log: A rice cake is pressed into your sleeve at the gate.

events.text: {b8oh_old_head} of {b8oh_house} has gone into the long dark, and the altar is shaken. The keepers cannot agree whom to follow. The able deputy {b8oh_head} stands left, a kinsman right, and every face turns to you, the {b8oh_rank}.

choices.text: Back {b8oh_head}, the able one

effects.log: You say the name aloud. The kinsman bows without bitterness. The incense steadies for the first time in a week.

choices.text: Back the old head's kin

effects.log: You choose blood over skill, and say so. The hall makes the soft sound of a heart being comforted.

events.text: A clerk of the Book of Fates arrives at {b8oh_house} with an empty line to fill by dusk, now that {b8oh_old_head} is gone. Two names are offered: {b8oh_head}, who is gifted, and a kinsman, who is beloved. The worshippers in the court have gone quiet, listening.

choices.text: Name the gifted one

effects.log: The clerk writes it. Whatever else, the altar will not run short of a firm hand.

choices.text: Name the beloved kinsman

effects.log: The clerk writes it with a blank face. Some say you chose out of tenderness. You let them.

events.text: A prayer-wind brings word that {b8oh_house} is {b8oh_step} now: the bowls half-empty, the roof wanting mending, the gate-spirit hoarse from calling worshippers who do not come. The note ends, in a tired hand, "if ever you are able."

choices.text: Send an anonymous gift of faith: {b8oh_help}

effects.log: You send it by wind without a name. The reply is full of guesses about the donor, nearly all wrong.

choices.text: Let it be

effects.log: Cults, like gods, rise and sink on their own tides. You do not read the last line again.

events.text: A pilgrim at your shrine mentions in passing that {b8oh_house} is {b8oh_step}. The smoke over the lower altar is thin, and a family of crows has taken the bell-tower. No one has asked anything of you.

choices.text: Send help unsigned: {b8oh_help}

effects.log: You give the pilgrim the offering to carry, as a gift from "a friend." That will do.

choices.text: Let it be

effects.log: You bless the pilgrim's road. The crows, you decide, mean the cult no harm.

events.text: A lesser god of ledgers waylays you on the cloud-road with news: {b8oh_house} is {b8oh_step}, and its offering-roll has been quietly struck from three worshippers' rosters. "Not my business," it adds, wringing its sleeves. "But I thought you would want to know."

choices.text: Send a gift of faith: {b8oh_help}

effects.log: The gift goes by the ledger-god's own hand. It swears to say it came from an anonymous well-wisher.

choices.text: Let it be

effects.log: You thank the god and move on. For a week you find yourself reading offering-rolls you have no reason to read.

events.text: The wind of dying altars brings the whisper: {b8oh_house} has fallen. The last incense is out and the gate-spirit has walked away. A passing minor god tells you as of a small matter. You thank it very evenly.

choices.text: Say the founder's name once, under your breath

effects.log: You say {b8oh_founder}, and the wind stills one breath. No god turns. The name goes like any other word.

choices.text: Look at the empty quarter a while

effects.log: A small light used to be there. It is only sky now.

events.text: At the hour of the offering-bell the bell does not ring. By dawn the Book of Fates has closed a page, and every ear in the pantheon has it: {b8oh_house} is gone, its faith scattered to other altars. Your morning cup is steady in your hand. The cup, for some reason, is not.

choices.text: Light one stick of the old blend

effects.log: The smoke goes straight up, then turns toward a place in the sky where nothing is.

choices.text: Say nothing of it to anyone

effects.log: At evening you find you have set out an extra bowl, and you let it sit.

events.text: The king's tax-registrar rides out with a long ledger and writes {b8oh_house} into the roll of free houses, grunting over the spelling. "For the levy and the record." Lower: "My grandmother said anything founded well gets written somewhere bigger than this book."

choices.text: Ask what bigger book she meant

effects.log: "The sky, she said. Or the Maker's." You leave the door open a while after.

choices.text: Pour the registrar a bowl of millet beer

effects.log: It goes down in one swallow. Your name is left in a neater hand than the rest of the page.

events.text: At the shrine of the Maker in the market square, the old priest ties a strip of red cloth to the rail for every house newly founded that season. This season there are four. One strip, the newest, bears the name {b8oh_house} in your own hand, which you do not remember giving.

choices.text: Tie a knot of your own beside it

effects.log: The priest nods as if that were the whole rite. The cloth lifts in the draught and settles.

choices.text: Ask the priest what the cloth is for

effects.log: "Remembering," says the priest. "The Maker, they say, forgets nothing. We do it in miniature."

events.text: A harvest-fair crowd spills into the yard of your new house, farmers' wives with baskets, a boy with a goat, a drunken fiddler. The fiddler plays something that makes you stop with a ladle in the air: a founding tune, nobody's, which you have clearly always known.

choices.text: Hum the second line

effects.log: The fiddler brightens, and plays it again for you. You do not have to be asked twice.

choices.text: Ask the fiddler where the tune came from

effects.log: "Dreamt it," says the fiddler. "Doesn't everyone?" He goes back to the goat.

events.text: The king's Registrar of Houses leans across his desk. "Ten houses in your name already, and every one still pulls. To enter {b8oh_house} I must strike a line, or leave it unentered. A soul can carry ten. Not eleven."

choices.text: Leave {b8oh_house} unentered

effects.log: The page is closed. The house will stand or fall without your name on its beam, and without owing you.

choices.text: Strike the faintest of the ten

effects.log: A thin line goes through it. Somewhere across the kingdom, a school you loved stops being yours.

events.text: In the Maker's shrine the priest lights ten tapers for you from the same flame and holds out an eleventh, for {b8oh_house}. They gutter together in the draught. "A flame can be shared ten ways before it dies," the priest says. "Which will you let go out?"

choices.text: Hold the eleventh taper back

effects.log: The priest snuffs it gently between two fingers. The house burns on elsewhere, owing you nothing.

choices.text: Pinch out the dimmest of the ten

effects.log: The smoke smells of a roof you once mended. You do not watch it rise.

choices.text: Ask the priest to keep it lit a season

effects.log: "A season, then," says the priest, and sets the taper in a niche behind the altar.

events.text: A grain carter, bragging of the farms on the south road, drops his voice at {b8oh_house}. "Founded by {b8oh_founder}, they say. {b8oh_gens} masters since. Strange place: the front hall is older than the rest, and the cooks all hum one song." You have never been. You know the song.

choices.text: Ask the carter to take you there

effects.log: He moves a sack. By dusk the school's roof rises over the barley, and your feet know the path.

choices.text: Ask him about the next town

effects.log: He tells you of an inn with good soup. The song stays with you all the way to the soup.

events.text: A herald is crying the roll of houses that sent grain to the king's granary this year. "...the household of {b8oh_house}, {b8oh_gens} heads old, which sent more than it could spare." A woman beside you mutters that they always do. She says it fondly. Your thumb is at your lip before you know.

choices.text: Ask her where it lies

effects.log: She points up the valley with a baby on her hip. "Follow the smoke. The fourth chimney."

choices.text: Listen to the rest of the roll

effects.log: The herald goes on to richer houses. You cannot quite recall what any of them were called.

events.text: A wandering scribe at the inn reads from his gazetteer for the price of a cup. "{b8oh_house}: a modest house. They keep one tablet above all others and will not say whose it is." The scribe looks up and sees you. "You are very still, friend."

choices.text: Say you were only listening

effects.log: The scribe goes back to his page. For the rest of the night you do not hear a word he reads.

choices.text: Ask the road to the school

effects.log: He gives it with the flourish of one who loves directions. You could now find it in the dark.

events.text: The tea bowl at the roadside stall has a glaze you know, and a potter's mark: the sign of {b8oh_house}. The stall-keeper says their pupils sell bowls at market to cover the roof-tax, and that the house is {b8oh_step}. You turn the bowl in the light as if it could be weighed.

choices.text: Ask where they fire them

effects.log: "Past the third mill, behind the poplar." You finish your tea very slowly.

choices.text: Buy two bowls and take the far road

effects.log: The bowls sit on your shelf, the house sits in your head, and neither speaks.

events.text: The porter of {b8oh_house} bows you into the front hall without asking your name. Above the hearth, set higher than the rest, stands a single tablet in lettering older than the house's oldest tree. It says {b8oh_founder}. Your breath leaves like a bellows with a hole in it.

choices.text: Give a guest's name and ask to sit

effects.log: The porter writes it down without glancing at the tablet, which you appreciate.

choices.text: Say the tablet is yours

effects.log: You say it aloud in the hall. The porter looks from the tablet to your face, and sends a boy running.

choices.text: Bow to the tablet and leave

effects.log: You bow as a stranger would, and once more as no stranger would. The road back is quiet, and not unkind.

events.text: The lane to {b8oh_house} is steep as you knew it would be, and your knees know where each worn step dips. At the top, children sweeping the threshold sing a counting song with, you are sure, a verse about you. Inside, the first tablet reads {b8oh_founder}.

choices.text: Ask for a seat among the guests

effects.log: A sweeper takes your sleeve and leads you in like a favourite aunt. You do not correct the child.

choices.text: Tell the sweepers who you were

effects.log: The children go quiet. The smallest, very carefully, says the founder died long ago. You say you know, and that it is a long story.

choices.text: Sweep a few leaves and go

effects.log: No one asks you to stay and no one asks you to go. At the lane's foot you find you are humming the verse.

events.text: Rain on the thatch, and the porter of {b8oh_house} comes out with a waxed-paper umbrella to look at you. "Whoever you are, the first tablet has been strangely warm since you set foot on our lane."

choices.text: Say you want only shelter from the rain

effects.log: The umbrella is held over you the length of the yard. You are seated by the brazier with a bowl of broth.

choices.text: Say the tablet knows you

effects.log: The porter's eyebrows rise and stay. "Then you will not mind if the masters ask a few questions."

choices.text: Thank the porter and go back into the rain

effects.log: The umbrella follows you to the gate, and stops. You do not look back, and feel it watching.

events.text: Harvest home at {b8oh_house}: the gate stands open, trestles fill the yard, strangers are fed. You eat and say little. Then the cups go round to the hearth, and every pupil pours a drop of wine before the first tablet. {b8oh_founder}. It is your own cup in your own hand.

choices.text: Stay and sit with the others

effects.log: Asked what you do, you say you have had many trades. They find that funny.

choices.text: Pour the drop with them and say the name

effects.log: The yard goes quiet. The name feels odd in your mouth, like a tooth that returned.

choices.text: Slip away before the second toast

effects.log: Three houses down the road the singing starts behind you. It is the founding song. You know the harmony.

events.text: The household of {b8oh_house} laughs until the old steward has to sit on a barrel. "The founder? Three founders this year already, and one of them was a goat-herd. The goat was better company." A pupil wipes tears with a sleeve. No one means harm. That is the worst of it.

choices.text: Laugh along, and say no more

effects.log: They like you better for it. Some part of you notes that this is how a tablet goes cold.

choices.text: Insist, loudly, in the hall

effects.log: Your voice rings under the beams. By noon you are shown the door with every courtesy and no appeal.

choices.text: Ask to see the first tablet again

effects.log: They let you, amused. Being laughed at hurts less once you have stood there.

events.text: A travelling tax-assessor, lodged at {b8oh_house} for the night, hears your claim at supper and writes it in his notebook as an entertainment. "Founder returned, in the person of a guest. The king's court will enjoy that." The table roars. Your soup has gone cold.

choices.text: Ask to read the entry

effects.log: You correct his spelling of the founder's name. He stops laughing, then starts again, more thinly.

choices.text: Tell him he will regret it

effects.log: You say it sharper than you meant. By morning your guest cot has been given to someone else.

events.text: The head master of {b8oh_house}, {b8oh_head}, does not laugh. A bowl of water, a brush and an old scroll with a gap in it are set before you. "The founder left a line unfinished. Finish it, and we shall see what you are."

choices.text: Write the line from memory

effects.log: The brush knows the stroke before you do. {b8oh_head} reads it, says nothing, and has the bowl taken away.

choices.text: Decline to be tested by a scroll

effects.log: You say a name should not need a brush. {b8oh_head} bows a hair lower than before.

choices.text: Ask what the line should say

effects.log: {b8oh_head} smiles for the first time. "That is the first wise thing a pretender has not done."

events.text: {b8oh_head} takes you out to the threshing floor of {b8oh_house} at dusk, where the founder, it is said, once settled a quarrel with a handful of barley. A sack is set before you, and a sieve. "Tell me what the founder did with these," says {b8oh_head}. "Not what is written. What was done."

choices.text: Answer from the heart

effects.log: You say the founder shared the sack out among the quarrellers and kept none, then sieved the chaff for the hens. {b8oh_head} lowers the sieve slowly.

choices.text: Say you do not remember, and it is true

effects.log: "Few say that," murmurs {b8oh_head}, and the dusk seems to settle a little kindlier.

events.text: The old porter of {b8oh_house} comes to you after the household has gone to bed, and kneels, which at that age is not easy. "I dusted the first tablet every morning for sixty years. It never moved the way it moved when you spoke. I believe you. So will they, by spring."

choices.text: Raise the porter and accept the belief

effects.log: You lift the porter by both elbows. From that night the house speaks of you as of a tide long due.

choices.text: Ask the porter to say nothing yet

effects.log: The porter keeps the secret for a month, a heroic length of time for a porter.

events.text: {b8oh_head} puts the scroll away before you have finished. "That is the founder's cadence. We changed the third beat of the song a hundred years ago, and nobody told me what it was before. You have just sung it." The household sits very still. One of them weeps into a harvest apron.

choices.text: Take the head's hand and let them believe

effects.log: Their voices return slowly, like geese. By evening a guest room is being aired for you.

choices.text: Say you are only a guest who knew the song

effects.log: {b8oh_head} nods slowly, as one nods to a kind lie, and does not forget it.

events.text: A king's herald has just confirmed the grain-levy of {b8oh_house}, and in the glow of it the household calls you to the front court. They offer you the rank of {b8oh_next}, a seat nearer the hearth and a voice in the spring accounts. A younger pupil watches, trying not to hope.

choices.text: Accept the rank

effects.log: You take it with both hands. The seat is harder than the guest bench, and the view of the gate from it is better.

choices.text: Decline, and put the younger pupil forward

effects.log: You push the paper across. The pupil is too stunned to speak. {b8oh_head} writes your word down.

choices.text: Decline, and stay as you are

effects.log: You say the guest bench suits you. The offer will not come twice soon.

events.text: The Maker's festival falls in the week the household of {b8oh_house} counts its lambs, and the count is good. {b8oh_head} fastens a new cord on your sleeve and says quietly that it was woven the year you first came, and raises you to {b8oh_next}.

choices.text: Wear the cord

effects.log: It is lighter than it looks. By dusk the whole yard uses your new title as though it had always been so.

choices.text: Ask whose hand wove it

effects.log: "The cook's," says {b8oh_head}. "Who is gone. The cook said you would be back."

choices.text: Hand it back with thanks

effects.log: {b8oh_head} puts it in a box clearly meant to wait.

events.text: The morning the household of {b8oh_house} raises you to {b8oh_next} is cold with ground fog. The cooks have baked a cake in the shape of the front gate, and set a small clay figure on top that is, unmistakably, you.

choices.text: Cut the cake and take the rank

effects.log: You cut the first slice for the porter. The rank settles over you like a warm coat, and fits.

choices.text: Thank them, and say not yet

effects.log: They are crestfallen for as long as it takes to pass the cake. Then they save the clay figure for you.

events.text: Spring accounts at {b8oh_house}. The ledger is short by more than the fields can grow back, and the household eyes you, the {b8oh_rank}, with the hope of people who do not like to ask. Damp lamps hiss. Nobody will say it first.

choices.text: Offer counsel on the accounts

effects.log: Three evenings with the abacus and the cook's receipts, and you find the leak. The household pretends to be surprised.

choices.text: Take a quiet cut from the guest fund

effects.log: No one stops you, because no one counts. The coin is yours by custom. The house is the poorer by it, and you know by how much.

choices.text: Say you have outstayed your welcome

effects.log: You bow to each in turn. The cook, at the back, weeps into a towel. You take the road at dawn.

events.text: The king's levy-men want twelve sons of {b8oh_house} for the border works, and the household is in uproar. The head turns to the {b8oh_rank}, who has seen the court at close range, and asks what is to be done. Twelve faces wait.

choices.text: Draft a petition and carry it yourself

effects.log: You walk to the provincial seat in two days. The levy is cut to five, and the household treats you like a hero for a month.

choices.text: Quietly point the levy-men at the neighbours

effects.log: The neighbours lose their sons instead. It is easy, and it is done, and you eat your supper with an effort.

choices.text: Say it is not your quarrel, and leave

effects.log: You go before the levy-men arrive. The household does not look at you as you pass.

events.text: A blight has crept into the barley of {b8oh_house}, and a pilgrim priest of the Maker's temple is passing by and offers, for a gift, to bless the field. The head is torn between faith and thrift. The {b8oh_rank}, at the table, is asked what the Maker would want.

choices.text: Advise sowing a second crop and blessing both

effects.log: Sound sense, mild piety. The blight spares half, the priest is paid, and the household thinks you wiser than you are.

choices.text: Advise the priest's blessing, and a portion for you

effects.log: A small commission, quietly. The blessing is real enough. The commission is not quite honest.

choices.text: Say the Maker is not your concern, and go

effects.log: You leave them to their blight and their priest. The road is dry and the barley behind you is yellow.

events.text: Winter, and the roof of {b8oh_house} leaks over the pupils' dormitory. Two masters want it patched with straw, one wants the whole timber replaced by spring, and none of them has the coin for either. The {b8oh_rank} is asked, as a courtesy, to settle it.

choices.text: Climb up and help patch it yourself

effects.log: You spend a week on the roof in a borrowed coat. The pupils bring you hot water in a pail, laughing.

choices.text: Take the guest fund and fund the timber

effects.log: The roof is saved. The guest fund is empty, and the fund was not exactly yours to spend.

choices.text: Say a guest should not settle a household's roof

effects.log: You thank them for the courtesy and take the morning cart. Behind you the roof drips on.

events.text: {b8oh_old_head} has gone, and the hall of {b8oh_house} is full of people who each want a different successor. They look at you, the {b8oh_rank}, whose word the old head valued. The able deputy {b8oh_head} stands to one side. A kinsman stands to the other.

choices.text: Back {b8oh_head}, the able one

effects.log: You say it plainly in the yard. The kinsman bows and does not hide his face. The house breathes out.

choices.text: Back the old head's kin

effects.log: Blood is blood, and the old head loved the child. The hall makes the sound a hall makes when it agrees with the heart.

events.text: The mourning drum has sounded for {b8oh_old_head}, and the king's clerk waits at the gate with the roll, wanting a name by dusk. Two are in the running: {b8oh_head}, who has the skill, and a kinsman, who has the blood. Beyond the gate, the village stands silent in the road.

choices.text: Name the skilled one

effects.log: The clerk writes it. The house will not drift for want of a hand on the oar.

choices.text: Name the kinsman

effects.log: The clerk writes it with a blank face. Some say you chose for love. You let them say it.

events.text: A letter reaches you by the carter's hand: {b8oh_house} is {b8oh_step} now. A fence has fallen. The cook has left. The spring levy is two months late, and the last line says only, "if ever you are able."

choices.text: Send what you can, unsigned: {b8oh_help}

effects.log: You send it without a name. The reply is full of guesses about the donor, and nearly all are wrong.

choices.text: Let it be

effects.log: Houses do what houses do, with or without you. You do not read the last line again.

events.text: A drover passing {b8oh_house} says it is {b8oh_step}. He says it plainly, as one reports weather. The well-rope has not been replaced in a season, and a family of owls has taken the grain loft. Nobody expects anything of you.

choices.text: Send help anonymously: {b8oh_help}

effects.log: You pay the drover to carry it. He says he will tell them it came from a friend of the school.

choices.text: Let it be

effects.log: You thank the drover and pay him for his news. The owls, you decide, will do the house no harm.

events.text: A pilgrim of the Maker's temple, resting at your door, mentions in passing that {b8oh_house} is {b8oh_step}: its altar-cloth moth-eaten, its wine-jar dry at the festival. The pilgrim says it kindly, the way one speaks of a distant cousin. You are not asked for anything.

choices.text: Send a gift for the temple-day: {b8oh_help}

effects.log: The pilgrim carries it, as a gift from "someone who remembers." You let that stand.

choices.text: Let it be

effects.log: You offer the pilgrim your best bread. The news stays in the room long after the pilgrim leaves.

events.text: The news comes on market day: {b8oh_house} has fallen. The roof is in, the yard is empty, and the last pupils have taken the road to other halls. A stranger tells it as one tells weather. At the end you thank him very evenly and ask the price of salt.

choices.text: Say the founder's name once, under your breath

effects.log: You say {b8oh_founder}, and the market keeps bargaining. Nobody turns. The name goes off on the wind like any other word.

choices.text: Look at the south road until it feels less

effects.log: You look a long time. It is not less. It is only road.

events.text: The Maker's priest reads the year's losses from the shrine step on feast day, house by house. When the name {b8oh_house} comes, no one in the crowd knows it. You do. You stand in the square and do not move until the reading is over and the crowd has gone.

choices.text: Tie a red cloth to the shrine rail for it

effects.log: The priest sees, and ties a second beside yours without a word. They hang together in the wind.

choices.text: Go home and speak of it to no one

effects.log: At evening you find you have set out an extra bowl, and you let it sit.
